Full current risk review: Checked all six proof steps against current finite-generator parabolic, exchange, subword, free-group and normal-closure statements. A normal-closure witness is a finite product; the free-group retraction makes its equality hold inside the finite support K. Finite parabolic injectivity then gives global injectivity. Length equality is proved before either direction of the Bruhat subword equivalence; both directions preserve reflection chains and fixed expressions. Empty J and w=1 yield the trivial subgroup and interval bound one. Reader additions in 1.1 are sound.

The original support-degree notation alpha was justified as the Schur exponent by the next lemma; the revised nu avoids anticipation. Full current risk review: Checked all eight steps against the explicit P hypotheses, not assumed conjecture truth. P15′ constant terms and P8 prove associativity; P2/P3/P5/P6/P7 give the identity and perfect trace. P15′ gives commuting layer actions, yielding the homomorphism and bimodule compatibility. Kernel elements raise the finite filtration, so N+1 products vanish after every base change; split generic semisimplicity then gives the dimension-preserving isomorphism. Rational evaluation of finitely many transported matrix units avoids zero and all denominator/determinant roots, giving rational splitting; central idempotents identify blocks up to relabeling. The current conclusion uses nu_E only for support, and does not assume nu_E=alpha_E. The restriction to nonzero evaluation is necessary for Laurent coordinates and is sound.

The inverse pairing tensor proves coefficient orthogonality locally. The stable lattice is a finite integer sum of rational images and is torsion-free, hence free over Z. Squaring the character congruences in the exact Hecke dual basis proves lowest coefficient f_E at −2nu_E, hence nu_E=alpha_E. Cayley–Hamilton plus the Laurent UFD puts the full Schur element in A. All field/ring extensions and zero-weight caveats are retained; specialized full Schur elements may vanish.

The original 3.1 already had alpha_E=a_M and alpha_E≥b, which together give b≤a_M; with a_M≤b this gives equality. The reader moves this routine inference explicitly into 2.2 using E(M) and expands the inherited simple-head argument. The exact original proof does not infer total multiplicity one merely from head multiplicity: reciprocity and the single J summand provide it. No fatal or nonfatal logical defect is confirmed by that explanatory expansion. Full current risk review: Checked all five steps and all eight cited facts against the now-reviewed supplier chain and Geck Theorem 6.6/Proposition 6.7 (geck.txt lines 2390–2551). A nonzero action on a composition factor implies nonzero action on the whole restricted V_E; P4 then gives a_M≤alpha_E. Asymptotic induction attains that bound. The first nonzero projective layer exists, is a quotient of the cover and inherits a superfluous maximal kernel, hence simple head and indecomposability. Its semisimple J decomposition can have only one summand. Reciprocity applied to E(M) gives the essential reverse inequality b≤a_M, so b=a_M, not merely equality of head multiplicity. This proves unique minimum and multiplicity one in the entire decomposition column. All hypotheses include AC, finite Weyl, generic splitting, nonnegative integral weights and P2–P8/P15′; only leading integers need survive specialization.
